findings.statement: the bulk segment writer ingests at least 1.25x the general writer, seal and partitioning inside the window
findings.detail: bulk 259014 ops/s against general 201976 (bulk vs general: greater 1.282x (p=0.0022, rel_iqr 7.1%/6.8%)) on 1000000 keys in 1000-record durable batches with the drain inside the window. Loop alone: 1.777s against 1.623s; commit phase 1.047s against 0.917s, seal 0.539s against 1.346s, merge 1.606s against 1.960s. f46 priced the writer's floor at 2.04x the general path on the seal alone (F46.1); this is the built writer, with the block table, checksums and superblock it omitted, on the load the engine is judged by

findings.statement: the seal phase is at least 1.8x faster with the bulk writer
findings.detail: seal phase 1.342s general against 0.537s bulk (general vs bulk: greater 2.501x (p=0.0009, rel_iqr 20.8%/7.9%)), as the engine accounts it. The memtable sort and the chain walk are the same in both arms; what differs is Store's hash table, freelist, pending arena and checkpoint against one forward pass. Merge phase, which writes through the same two writers: 1.960s against 1.606s

findings.statement: bulk segments take at most 0.9x the disk of general ones
findings.detail: 180.2 MB on disk with the bulk writer against 190.6 with the general one (0.945x) for 110.6 MB of records; device bytes 491.0 against 472.7 MB. A bulk segment has no freelist rounding, no reuse log, no redo-log arena and no index slack. Space is immune to drift, so this ratio is a plain median ratio

findings.statement: reads over the loaded store do not differ between the writers
findings.detail: 200000 random point reads after the drain: bulk 1234347/s against general 1090971/s (bulk vs general: greater 1.131x (p=0.0054, rel_iqr 5.3%/3.5%)). Segments after the drain, partitioned + L0: bulk 3+0 against general 3+0. Same format, same Blob, same routing; a difference either way means the writers lay blocks down differently or the drain leaves a different layout behind

findings.statement: the merge phase is at least 1.5x faster finding keys by rank cursors than by probes, same writer
findings.detail: merge phase 1.573s with the probe merge against 1.206s with rank cursors (probes vs cursors: greater 1.305x (p=0.0009, rel_iqr 8.6%/8.0%)), both writing through SegmentWriter. The probe merge collects every key into a vector, sorts and deduplicates it, then probes each input's index once per key; the cursor merge walks each input's key section forwards once and hashes nothing

findings.statement: ingest-to-routed with the cursor merge is at least 1.15x the bulk arm's
findings.detail: bulk-cursors 286055 ops/s against bulk 259014 (bulk-cursors vs bulk: greater 1.104x (p=0.0152, rel_iqr 2.9%/7.1%)); seal 0.542s against 0.539s, merge 1.228s against 1.606s, device bytes 491.0 against 491.0 MB, disk 180.2 against 180.2 MB. Against the general arm's 201976 ops/s the shipping configuration is 1.416x

findings.statement: reads after the drain do not differ between the probe and cursor merges, same writer
findings.detail: bulk-cursors 1218131/s against bulk 1234347/s (bulk-cursors vs bulk: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 0.987, p=0.7929) -- within noise, not a result); segments after the drain 3+0 against 3+0. Same writer, same blocks; only how the inputs were walked differs. The control for F49.4: if these tie and the segment counts match, the read difference against general is the writer's layout or the drain's, not the merge's

notes: two arms interleaved in one process, fresh store per rep, the f42 load shape (durable per batch, partitioning on). The arms differ only in NextOptions::bulk_writer and cursor_merge: general writes every piece through Store::create/append/checkpoint/close and finds merge keys by collect-sort-probe, bulk writes through SegmentWriter with the same probe merge, bulk-cursors adds the k-way rank merge (the shipping default). The timed window is the load PLUS the drain (flush: seal, join, partition), the shape the external suite times, because on the loop alone the seal overlaps the commits and most of its cost is hidden (F42.3). load_s is the loop by itself. Device bytes from /proc/self/io over the window; disk bytes are the store's files after close; the read sample runs after the drain, so every key is sealed and routed in both arms
